text:
Mark Jankowski has 10 goals in 18 games. His previous best for a full season, by our data, was 11 last year, when Carolina won the Stanley Cup. Two of them came in the Global Series win over Seattle on Nov. 14, the second set up by Taylor Hall.

Enjoy it while it lasts, because the finishing won't. He's shooting 27% against 17% last season and has scored about four more goals than his chances say he should. The chances themselves are real: 5.9 expected goals is a strong number for a 32-year-old on 14 and a half minutes a night, and that's what keeps this from being a pure fluke.

His actual job is defensive. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 92nd percentile at taking chances away last season, with most of his value coming from even-strength defense, and it noted his 0.6 wins lagged 1.6 expected because the pucks didn't go in. This year they are. The strange part: Carolina's five-on-five numbers are better without him, about six points of expected goal share. What to watch is his ice time once the goals slow.
